audits.title: EP.FRI.34 Audit of management of shoulder dislocations against BOA Traumatic anterior shoulder instability Guidelines
audits.standard: BOA 2015 traumatic anterior shoulder instability guidelines

cycle1.result: 88% had AP and lateral x-rays; 8.9% pre-reduction AP only; 11.9% no pre-reduction x-ray; 1.5% no post-reduction imaging; 79% seen in clinic within 6 weeks; 40.3% seen by a shoulder specialist; 43.3% had appropriate imaging; 16.4% not given fracture clinic follow-up.

audits.intervention: Suggested: rename fracture clinics by subspecialty and a session reviewing the guideline with senior surgeons.
audits.other_findings: Acute management mostly compliant; follow-up and later investigation were weaker.
audits.citation: Varasteh A, Hakim Z. EP.FRI.34 Audit of management of shoulder dislocations against BOA Traumatic anterior shoulder instability Guidelines. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab312.007.

audits.title: 174 An Audit on First Time Shoulder Dislocations: Are We Following BESS Guidelines?
audits.standard: BESS guidelines for first-time shoulder dislocation
audits.setting: Emergency department, Birmingham Heartlands Hospital (large acute general hospital)

cycle1.result: 85% seen in fracture clinic but only 25% seen by a consultant; 40% had appropriate imaging requested; 50% correctly referred to a shoulder surgeon or shoulder clinic.

audits.intervention: Pathway designed so all first-time dislocations are followed up in fracture clinic with timely investigations (not yet re-audited).
audits.other_findings: A large number of concomitant injuries were found; most patients were seen by a physiotherapist.
audits.citation: Tariq F, Remtulla M, Jordan R. 174 An Audit on First Time Shoulder Dislocations: Are We Following BESS Guidelines?. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac039.105.

audits.title: Shoulder Reduction Bench Project: improving care for patients with shoulder dislocations.
audits.standard: Royal College of Emergency Medicine guidelines on time to shoulder dislocation reduction (2-hour RCEM clinical standard of 75% for initial attempt at reduction)
audits.setting: Emergency department, City Hospitals Sunderland NHS Foundation Trust; district general hospital, adults 16 and over

cycle1.result: Average triage to confirmed shoulder reduction X-ray 2 hours 25 min (range 1 h 14 min to 5 h 3 min); triage to discharge 3 hours 22 min (range 1 h 46 min to 6 h 39 min); 57% (17/30) sedated for reduction.

audits.intervention: Shoulder Reduction Bench (modified Oxford Chair) introduced with three PDSA cycles: training of emergency nurse practitioners, written protocol and flowchart on the intranet, and an online training video.

cycle2.period: 6 months after project launch (March to September)
cycle2.result: Average triage to confirmed reduction X-ray 1 hour 54 min (31 min, 21% reduction); triage to discharge 2 hours 30 min (52 min, 26% reduction); 18% (7) sedated, a 68% reduction.

audits.other_findings: The protocol was not followed in 2 cases (5%, both consultants) and adherence was unclear in 2 more; after restricting use to protocol criteria there were no further complications.
audits.citation: Dowson P. Shoulder Reduction Bench Project: improving care for patients with shoulder dislocations. BMJ Open Qual. 2019;8(2):e000366. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2018-000366. PMID: 31276053.

audits.title: A Retrospective Audit of the Management of Shoulder Dislocations at a Trauma Unit.
audits.standard: Health board clinical pathway for traumatic anterior shoulder instability, aligned with BOA and BESS guidance (pre- and post-reduction radiographs, neurovascular assessment, specialist follow-up)
audits.setting: Emergency department and trauma unit, The Grange University Hospital, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board

cycle1.result: Pre- and post-reduction radiographs in 97/100 (97%), post-reduction only in 3 (3%); MUA successful in 98 (98%); mean time to reduction 152 minutes; nerve injury in 28 (28%)

audits.other_findings: Not all patients under 40 received an MR arthrogram as recommended. Posterior dislocations made up 16% of cases and 10 patients were lost to follow-up.
audits.citation: Mansoor M, Datta S, Bandyopadhyay B, Madhu R, Raza MT, Hussain MW, et al.. A Retrospective Audit of the Management of Shoulder Dislocations at a Trauma Unit. Cureus. 2025;17(7):e87256. doi:10.7759/cureus.87256. PMID: 40761982.

audits.title: Orthogonal Radiographs After Shoulder Reduction: Are We Meeting the Standard?
audits.standard: BESS guideline and local hospital policy: orthogonal post-reduction views (AP plus axillary or scapular Y view)
audits.setting: Emergency department, Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham (tertiary centre)

cycle1.result: Adequate orthogonal post-reduction radiographs in 5/22 (22.7%, 95% CI 10.1-43.4); 17/22 (77.3%) inadequate, with inadequacy recognised by resident doctors in 2/17 (11.8%).

audits.other_findings: No imaging request explicitly specified two orthogonal views and no repeat imaging was obtained in the ED; education and re-audit are planned.
audits.citation: Mahajan U, Yousaf M, Jinadu K, Memon K. Orthogonal Radiographs After Shoulder Reduction: Are We Meeting the Standard?. Cureus. 2025;17(10):e94814. doi:10.7759/cureus.94814. PMID: 41250712.
